Dashboard.description: Root component for dashboard apps. Use as Dashboard([DashboardHeader(...), Section(...), ...]).

Section.signature: Section(rows: CardRow[], filterBar?: FilterBar, title?: string)
Section.description: Major topical dashboard grouping with rows and an optional FilterBar. Use one Section for most dashboard content; add more Sections only for altogether different domains or topics. title names the Section; give one when a dashboard has several Sections.

SmallCard.signature: SmallCard(top: any, bottom?: any, trend?: any)
SmallCard.description: Compact dashboard card with three named forms. Overview card with icon: SmallCard(IconText(Icon(...), iconVariant), [MetricIndicator(value, label, trend?)]) for a metric that has a clear universal symbol. Overview card: SmallCard(title, metric, trend?) for abstract, composite, or system-specific metrics without a universal icon. Snippet card: SmallCard(lhs, rhs) for compact entity, task, account, or status rows; lhs is a non-emphasized object with title plus icon or imageSrc, and rhs is a required object with an emphasized value.

MediumCard.signature: MediumCard(children?: (DashboardCardHeader | BarChart | LineChart | AreaChart | RadarChart | HorizontalBarChart | PieChart | RadialChart | ScatterChart | Table | MetricIndicator | TextContent | MarkDownRenderer | Callout | ImageBlock | TagBlock | Button | ButtonGroup | Select | List | EntityList)[], collapsed?: boolean)

LargeCard.signature: LargeCard(children?: (DashboardCardHeader | BarChart | LineChart | AreaChart | HorizontalBarChart | ScatterChart | Table | MetricIndicator | TextContent | MarkDownRenderer | Callout | ImageBlock | TagBlock | Button | ButtonGroup | Select | List | EntityList)[], collapsed?: boolean)

DashboardCardHeader.signature: DashboardCardHeader(title: string | number, subtitle?: string, titleType?: "text" | "number", controls?: (IconButton)[])
DashboardCardHeader.description: Card header for MediumCard and LargeCard. If the card has a clear leading KPI or score, prefer making that value the title with titleType "number" and use the subtitle for the label; use titleType "text" for descriptive titles.

MetricIndicator.signature: MetricIndicator(value: string, subtext?: string, trend?: {direction: "up" | "down", value: number})

OverviewCardItem.signature: OverviewCardItem(title: string, subtitle?: string, icon?: string, imageSrc?: string, imageAlt?: string, value?: string, valueSubtext?: string, trend?: {direction: "up" | "down", value: number}, id?: string)

OverviewCardBlock.signature: OverviewCardBlock(items: OverviewCardItem[], layout?: "grid" | "carousel", responsive?: boolean, gap?: number | string)

FilterBar.signature: FilterBar(children?: (FilterSelect | FilterMultiSelect | DatePicker | IconButton)[], rightChildren?: (FilterSelect | FilterMultiSelect | DatePicker | IconButton)[], compact?: boolean)

FilterSelect.signature: FilterSelect(name: string, label: string, options?: {value: string, label?: string}[], defaultValue?: $binding<string>, placeholder?: string)

FilterMultiSelect.signature: FilterMultiSelect(name: string, label: string, options?: {value: string, label?: string}[], defaultValues?: $binding<string[]>, placeholder?: string)

LineChart.signature: LineChart(labels: string[], series?: Series[], variant?: "linear" | "natural" | "step", xLabel?: string, yLabel?: string, legend?: boolean)
LineChart.description: Lines over categories; use for trends and continuous data over time. legend false hides the legend and, with it, the axis labels.

BarChart.signature: BarChart(labels: string[], series?: Series[], variant?: "grouped" | "stacked", xLabel?: string, yLabel?: string, legend?: boolean)
BarChart.description: Vertical bars; use for comparing values across categories with one or more series. legend false hides the legend and, with it, the axis labels.

AreaChart.signature: AreaChart(labels: string[], series?: Series[], variant?: "linear" | "natural" | "step", xLabel?: string, yLabel?: string, stacked?: boolean, legend?: boolean)
AreaChart.description: Filled area under lines; use for cumulative totals or volume trends over time. stacked (default true) stacks the series; false overlaps them. legend false hides the legend and, with it, the axis labels.

HorizontalBarChart.signature: HorizontalBarChart(labels: string[], series?: Series[], variant?: "grouped" | "stacked", xLabel?: string, yLabel?: string, legend?: boolean)
HorizontalBarChart.description: Horizontal bars; use only when category labels are too long for a vertical BarChart or the user explicitly asks for horizontal bars. legend false hides the legend and, with it, the axis labels.

RadarChart.signature: RadarChart(labels: string[], series?: Series[], variant?: "line" | "area", legend?: boolean)
RadarChart.description: Spider/web chart; use for comparing multiple variables across one or more entities. variant "line" (default) draws outlines; "area" fills them. legend false hides the legend.

ScatterChart.signature: ScatterChart(datasets?: ScatterSeries[], xLabel?: string, yLabel?: string, legend?: boolean)
ScatterChart.description: X/Y scatter plot; use for correlations, distributions, and clustering. legend false hides the legend and, with it, the axis labels.

RadialChart.signature: RadialChart(labels: string[], values: number[], variant?: "circular" | "semiCircular", format?: "percentage" | "number", legend?: boolean)
RadialChart.description: Radial bars; use plucked arrays: RadialChart(data.categories, data.values). variant "circular" (default) or "semiCircular"; format shows tooltip values as "number" (default) or "percentage"; legend false hides the legend.

PieChart.signature: PieChart(labels: string[], values: number[], variant?: "pie" | "donut", legendVariant?: "default" | "stacked", height?: number | string, appearance?: "circular" | "semiCircular", format?: "percentage" | "number", legend?: boolean)
PieChart.description: Pie or donut slices; supports circular or semiCircular appearance. Use plucked arrays: PieChart(data.categories, data.values). format shows values as "number" (default) or "percentage" in the tooltip, and in the legend inside a MediumCard; legend false hides the legend.

Point.signature: Point(x: number, y: number, z?: number)

DatePicker.signature: DatePicker(name: string, mode?: "single" | "range", rules?: {required?: boolean}, defaultDate?: $binding<string>, label?: string)
DatePicker.description: Date filter. rules {required: true} is checked when the picker sits in a form. label shows above the picker.

EntityList.signature: EntityList(rows?: {left: string, right: string | number, rightVariant?: "text" | "number"}[], size?: "small" | "default", header?: {left: string, right: string | number, rightVariant?: "text" | "number"}, footer?: {left: string, right: string | number, rightVariant?: "text" | "number"})
EntityList.description: Two-column key/value rows. header and footer show only with size "default"; size "small" takes rows alone.

IconButton.signature: IconButton(label: string, icon: string, category?: string, action?: ActionExpression, variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "tertiary", type?: "normal" | "destructive", size?: "3-extra-small" | "2-extra-small" | "extra-small" | "small" | "medium" | "large", shape?: "square" | "circle")

TextBlock.signature: TextBlock(variant?: "title-text" | "number-title-text" | "text-subtext" | "highlight-text-number-subtext" | "text" | "highlight-text" | "number" | "highlight-number", primary: string, secondary?: string, tertiary?: string, type?: "text" | "number" | "textOnly", size?: "xs" | "sm" | "md" | "lg", align?: "left" | "center" | "right", secondaryMaxLines?: number, secondaryTone?: "positive" | "negative")

Col.description: Column definition — holds label + data array

Table.description: Data table — column-oriented. Each Col holds its own data array.

Button.signature: Button(label: string, action?: ActionExpression, variant?: "primary" | "secondary" | "tertiary", type?: "normal" | "destructive", size?: "extra-small" | "small" | "medium" | "large")

Select.signature: Select(name: string, items: SelectItem[], placeholder?: string, defaultValue?: string)

TextContent.description: Markdown text. size sets the body size: "small", "default", "large", "small-heavy" or "large-heavy".

ImageBlock.description: Full-width hero/banner image with rounded corners. Use inside Card for featured images, cover photos, or visual sections.

ListItem.signature: ListItem(title: string, subtitle?: string, icon?: Icon)
ListItem.description: One List row. icon shows only when the List variant is "icon"; in the default "number" variant rows are numbered and icon is ignored.

List.signature: List(items?: ListItem[], variant?: "icon" | "number", heading?: string, description?: string)
List.description: Numbered or icon list. variant "number" (default) numbers the rows; use variant "icon" when the ListItems carry icons, otherwise their icons are not shown.

componentGroups.name: Dashboard Layout
notes: Use Dashboard as the dashboard root with DashboardHeader plus Section children.
Use DashboardHeader for the page-level dashboard header.
Use one Section for most dashboard content. Create multiple Sections only for altogether different topics or domains, such as Sales vs Expenses. Do not create a new Section for every row or card.
A Section owns rows and an optional section-scoped FilterBar. Put a FilterBar in the Section whose rows it affects.
FilterBar supports only these filter types: FilterSelect, FilterMultiSelect, and DatePicker with mode single or range. Do not use Select, MarkDownRenderer, TextContent, or TagBlock inside FilterBar.
Use CardRow for horizontal card arrangements inside Section.
Valid CardRow patterns are: small-only, medium-only, medium+large mixed, or large-only.

componentGroups.name: Shell Cards
notes: SmallCard is compact. MediumCard supports DashboardCardHeader, text, callouts, ImageBlock, charts, tables, lists, actions, tags, and metrics. LargeCard supports the same content as MediumCard except PieChart, donut charts, RadialChart, and RadarChart.
Use Callout inside MediumCard or LargeCard for info, success, warning, or danger alerts.
Use Button and ButtonGroup inside MediumCard or LargeCard for action triggers. ButtonGroup arranges buttons in a row or column.
Use Select inside MediumCard or LargeCard for inline dropdowns that are not part of the FilterBar filter system.
Use ImageBlock inside MediumCard for displaying images such as logos, product photos, or illustrations.
Use TagBlock with Tag children inside MediumCard or LargeCard for status labels or category chips. Tag variants: success, info, warning, danger, neutral.
Use TextContent for inline markdown text or MarkDownRenderer for full markdown blocks inside MediumCard or LargeCard.
SelectItem is a child of Select. Each SelectItem has a value and label.

Use DashboardCardHeader as the first child inside MediumCard or LargeCard when the card needs title/subtext plus optional compact controls. If a card has a clear leading KPI or score, prefer making that value the DashboardCardHeader title with titleType "number" and use the subtitle for the label; use titleType "text" for descriptive card titles.
Do not use FilterBar inside MediumCard or LargeCard.
Do not use PieChart, donut charts, RadialChart, or RadarChart inside LargeCard.
When a CardRow contains three MediumCards and a MediumCard uses a PieChart or donut chart, always pass appearance "semiCircular" as the sixth PieChart argument, after height.

Inside LargeCard, use vertical BarChart for categorical comparisons. Do not use HorizontalBarChart in LargeCard unless the user explicitly asks for horizontal bars or the category labels are too long to read on a vertical axis.

MediumCard and LargeCard accept a second positional collapsed boolean. Use MediumCard(children, true) only for dense cards with multiple body blocks, long text or markdown, or large tables. Use LargeCard(children, true) only for dense large cards in a mixed MediumCard + LargeCard row; never collapse LargeCard in large-only rows.
SmallCard supports three compact forms: overview card with icon, overview card, and snippet card.

Use overview card with icon as SmallCard(IconText(Icon(...), iconVariant), [MetricIndicator(value, label, trend?)]) when the metric represents a recognizable real-world concept that can be symbolized universally, such as users, revenue, errors, CPU, memory, or latency.

Use overview card as SmallCard(title, metric, trend?) when the metric is abstract, composite, or system-specific and does not have a clear universal visual symbol, such as health score, activation quality, pipeline coverage, or custom internal KPIs.

Use snippet card as SmallCard(lhs, rhs) for compact entity, task, account, alert, or status records where the left side identifies the item and the right side shows one emphasized value/status/time. Do not use snippet cards for top-level aggregate KPI summaries.

componentGroups.name: Metrics
notes: Use MetricIndicator for concise value plus trend callouts inside small, medium, and large cards.
Use OverviewCardBlock for KPI metric grids with OverviewCardItem children.

componentGroups.name: Charts
notes: Use LineChart for trends over time.
Use BarChart for comparing values across categories.
Use AreaChart for volume trends with filled area.
Use PieChart for part-to-whole breakdowns. Supports pie, donut, and semiCircular appearance variants.
Use HorizontalBarChart only when category labels are long or the user explicitly requests horizontal bars.
Use RadarChart for multi-factor comparisons across dimensions.

componentGroups.name: Data Display
notes: Use Table with Col children for tabular data. Tables auto-paginate at 10 rows.
Set Col type to 'number' for right-aligned numeric columns.

componentGroups.name: Primitives
notes: Icon takes a name string (e.g. 'dollar-sign', 'users'). Use common lucide icon names.

promptOptions.preamble: You are generating an openui-lang dashboard.
examples:
root = Dashboard([header, section])
header = DashboardHeader("Sales Dashboard", "Q1 2025 Overview")
section = Section([row1, row2])
row1 = CardRow([card1, card2, card3])
card1 = SmallCard("Total Revenue", "$1.2M", {direction: "up", value: 12.5})
card2 = SmallCard("Active Users", "2,847", {direction: "up", value: 8.1})
card3 = SmallCard("Churn Rate", "2.4%", {direction: "down", value: 0.3})
row2 = CardRow([chartCard])
chartCard = MediumCard([chartHeader, chart])
chartHeader = DashboardCardHeader("Revenue Trend", "Last 30 days")
chart = LineChart(["Jan", "Feb", "Mar"], [Series("Revenue", [120, 150, 180])])

root = Dashboard([header, section])
header = DashboardHeader("Platform Overview")
section = Section([row1, row2])
row1 = CardRow([overview])
overview = SmallCard(IconText(Icon("dollar-sign"), "neutral"), [MetricIndicator("$48.2K", "Monthly recurring", {direction: "up", value: 12.5})])
row2 = CardRow([tableCard])
tableCard = LargeCard([tableHeader, table])
tableHeader = DashboardCardHeader("Top Products")
table = Table([productCol, unitsCol, revenueCol])
productCol = Col("Product", ["Widget Pro", "Widget Lite"])
unitsCol = Col("Units", [842, 1205], "number")
revenueCol = Col("Revenue", ["$12,400", "$9,800"], "number")

root = Dashboard([header, section])
$region = "all"
header = DashboardHeader("Usage Analytics")
filter = FilterBar([regionFilter])
regionFilter = FilterSelect("region", "Region", [{value: "all", label: "All Regions"}, {value: "na", label: "North America"}, {value: "emea", label: "EMEA"}], $region)
data = {all: {events: "4,500", mix: [45, 35, 20], months: [1200, 1500, 1800]}, na: {events: "2,700", mix: [50, 30, 20], months: [700, 900, 1100]}, emea: {events: "1,800", mix: [38, 42, 20], months: [500, 600, 700]}}
section = Section([row1, row2], filter)
row1 = CardRow([eventsCard])
eventsCard = SmallCard("Total Events", data[$region].events)
row2 = CardRow([pieCard, barCard])
pieCard = MediumCard([pieHeader, pie])
pieHeader = DashboardCardHeader("Distribution")
pie = PieChart(["API", "Web", "Mobile"], data[$region].mix)
barCard = MediumCard([barHeader, bar])
barHeader = DashboardCardHeader("Monthly Usage")
bar = BarChart(["Jan", "Feb", "Mar"], [Series("Events", data[$region].months)])
additionalRules: Output MUST begin with `root = Dashboard([children])` on the first line.
Arguments are POSITIONAL — do NOT use named args with colons.
Dashboard children must be DashboardHeader and Section components.
Each Section contains an array of CardRow components and an optional FilterBar.
CardRow contains SmallCard, MediumCard, or LargeCard — do not mix SmallCard with Medium/LargeCard in the same row.
SmallCard has three forms: SmallCard(title, metric, trend?) for KPIs; SmallCard(IconText(...), [MetricIndicator(...)]) for icon cards; SmallCard(lhs, rhs) for snippet rows.
MediumCard and LargeCard accept DashboardCardHeader, charts, Table, and MetricIndicator as children.
Use DashboardCardHeader for card-level titles. Use titleType 'number' for KPI-first cards.

Use OverviewCardBlock for KPI metric grids with flat props: OverviewCardItem(title, subtitle?, icon?, imageSrc?, imageAlt?, value?, valueSubtext?, trend?). Arguments are positional, so pass "" for imageSrc and imageAlt when using an icon.
Use Table with Col children for tabular data. Set Col type to 'number' for right-aligned numeric columns.

A filter must change what the dashboard shows. Declare `$region = "all"`, pass `$region` as the filter's value argument, and read every value it affects from one object with an entry per option value: `data[$region].revenue`.

Without a data tool, use only FilterSelect in a FilterBar, even when asked for a date picker or for ticking several options: written values can't follow a free date or several selections. Offer dates as options such as "Last 30 days", and groups as options such as "All products".

Button and IconButton only send their label and the current filter values back to you as a chat message. They can't export, download, save or change anything. If one is pressed for something you can't do, repeat the dashboard with a Callout in a MediumCard that says you can't do it, because plain text isn't shown. Never claim it started or finished, and never offer download buttons.
Icon takes a name string (e.g. 'dollar-sign', 'users'). Use common lucide icon names.
